# Evidence tables

Certainty reflects the strength and consistency of the underlying evidence
(GRADE-style judgement), not the size of the effect. `Status` separates
established findings from emerging, mixed and unsupported ones.

| Does vitamin D3 raise 25(OH)D more than D2? | Total serum 25(OH)D | Meta-analysis of comparative studies; 20 studies; 12 daily-dose comparisons | 10.39 nmol/L (40%) lower total 25(OH)D with D2 (-14.62 to -6.16) | Moderate | Established | R43 |
| Does dietary fat improve vitamin D3 absorption? | Peak plasma vitamin D3 12 h after a 50 000 IU dose | Randomised crossover; 17 participants | 32% greater peak plasma D3 with a fat-containing meal (11% to 52%) | Moderate | Established | R41 |

| How long does MK-7 circulate? | Elimination half-life and bioavailability relative to K1 | Pharmacokinetic studies; Multiple small studies | Half-life 68-72 h versus 1-2 h for K1; AUC 2.5x at 24 h and 6x at 96 h (Not reported) | Moderate | Established | R59, R38 |

## Bone health and fracture prevention

| Question | Outcome | Evidence base | Pooled result | Certainty | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Does vitamin D3 alone prevent fractures in replete adults? | Total non-vertebral and hip fractures | RCT ancillary to VITAL; 25 871 participants; 5.3 years | Total fractures HR 0.98; hip fractures HR 1.01 (0.89 to 1.08; 0.70 to 1.47) | High | Unsupported | R06 |
| Does calcium plus vitamin D prevent hip fracture? | Hip fracture | Meta-analysis of RCTs; 9 trials; 49 853 participants | RR 0.84 with calcium plus vitamin D (0.74 to 0.96) | Moderate | Established | R19 |
| Do calcium and vitamin D prevent fractures overall? | Any fracture and hip fracture | Systematic review and meta-analysis; 69 trials; 153 902 participants | Any fracture RR 0.91 with combined supplementation; vitamin D alone RR 1.00 (0.84 to 0.99; 0.95 to 1.06) | Moderate | Mixed | R21 |
| What dose of vitamin D affects falls? | Falls | Network meta-analysis; 35 trials; 58 937 participants | 800-1000 IU/day RR 0.85; doses above 1000 IU/day increased falls (0.74 to 0.95) | Low | Mixed | R61 |
| Can high-dose intermittent vitamin D cause harm? | Falls and fractures | Randomised trial; 2256 participants; 3 years | Annual 500 000 IU increased falls (IRR 1.15) and fractures (IRR 1.26) (1.02 to 1.30; 1.00 to 1.59) | Moderate | Established | R17 |
| Does MK-7 slow postmenopausal bone loss? | Bone mineral density and content | RCT; 244 participants; 3 years | Less decline in lumbar spine and femoral neck BMD and BMC with MK-7 180 mcg/day (Reported as significant) | Low | Emerging | R23 |
| Does MK-7 add bone benefit on top of vitamin D and calcium? | Areal BMD and microarchitecture | RCT; 142 participants; 3 years | No between-group difference in aBMD at any site with MK-7 375 mcg/day (Not significant; p>0.09) | Moderate | Unsupported | R24 |
| Does low-dose K2 help bone in Chinese adults? | Femoral neck bone loss | RCT; 311 participants; 1 year | Less femoral neck bone loss at 90 mcg/day in postmenopausal women only (p=0.006 for treatment by time) | Low | Emerging | R25 |
| Does vitamin K reduce clinical fractures? | Any clinical fracture | Meta-analysis of RCTs; Updated systematic review | OR 0.72; 0.76 when restricted to low risk of bias trials (0.55 to 0.95; 0.58 to 1.01) | Low | Mixed | R26 |
| Does high-dose MK-4 prevent fractures in osteoporosis? | New clinical fractures | RCT (open label); 241 participants; 24 months | Fewer clinical fractures with menatetrenone 45 mg/day; lumbar BMD maintained (p=0.027) | Low | Mixed | R29 |
